prompt: Use GitHub to inspect accessible repositories and branches, fetch repository files, update multiple repository files, create a public static preview repository, enable GitHub Pages, and commit generated content/configuration files.

results.use_case: Use GitHub to inspect accessible repositories and branches, fetch repository files, update multiple repository files, create a public static preview repository, enable GitHub Pages, and commit generated content/configuration files.
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if avoiding duplicates)] [Prerequisite]: Scan existing repositories using GITHUB_LIST_REPOSITORIES_FOR_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER (paginate until the intended repository is located).
[Optional (if the repository is missing)] [Step]: Create a repository using GITHUB_CREATE_A_REPOSITORY_FOR_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER (choose visibility and initialization settings up front).
[Required] [Prerequisite]: Read repository metadata using GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY (capture default branch and current configuration).
[Required] [Step]: Confirm the publish folder and entry content exist using GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT (check the chosen branch and site root or a docs-style subfolder).
[Fallback (if content is not found)] [Fallback]: Re-check the branch choice using GITHUB_LIST_BRANCHES, then retry validation using GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT.
[Required] [Step]: Enable or update static-site hosting using GITHUB_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_GITHUB_PAGES_SITE (select source branch and source path).
[Optional (if the repository is empty or missing site files)] [Step]: Add initial site files in a single commit using GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES (ensure an entry file exists at the publish path).
[Optional (for verification)] [Next Step]: Monitor the hosting build using GITHUB_GET_GITHUB_PAGES_BUILD until it reaches a terminal state.
known_pitfalls: [GITHUB_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_GITHUB_PAGES_SITE] Site enablement can be asynchronous (e.g., building); verify completion via GITHUB_GET_GITHUB_PAGES_BUILD rather than assuming immediate readiness.
[GITHUB_CREATE_A_REPOSITORY_FOR_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER] Responses can be very large; avoid returning or logging the full raw payload.
[GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT] Not-found errors are commonly caused by an incorrect branch or publish path; validate the exact folder/entry location before enabling hosting.
[GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES] New repositories may have no usable publish content; create the minimal required entry file(s) before expecting hosting to succeed.

toolkit_connection_statuses.description: GitHub is a code hosting platform for version control and collaboration, offering Git-based repository management, issue tracking, and continuous integration features

GITHUB_CREATE_A_REPOSITORY_FOR_THE_AUTHE.description: Creates a new repository for the authenticated user, optionally within an organization if `team_id` is specified.

name.description: The name of the repository. Must be unique within your account. Will be used in the repository URL (github.com/username/repo-name). Can only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, underscores, and periods.

private.description: Whether the repository is private (true) or public (false).

team_id.description: The ID of the team to be granted access. Only valid if creating in an organization.

homepage.description: A URL with more information about the repository.

auto_init.description: Whether to initialize the repository with a README.

examples: This is a project about X.
description.description: A short description of the repository.

is_template.description: Whether this repository is a template repository.

has_downloads.description: Whether downloads are enabled (deprecated by GitHub and may not be configurable).

allow_auto_merge.description: Whether to allow auto-merge on pull requests.

license_template.description: SPDX license key identifier (lowercase). Examples: 'mit', 'apache-2.0', 'gpl-3.0'. Must be one of the GitHub-supported licenses.

allow_merge_commit.description: Whether to allow merging pull requests with a merge commit.

allow_rebase_merge.description: Whether to allow rebase-merging pull requests.

allow_squash_merge.description: Whether to allow squash-merging pull requests.

merge_commit_title.description: The default title for a merge commit. `PR_TITLE` uses the pull request's title. `MERGE_MESSAGE` uses a classic title like 'Merge pull request #123 from branch-name'. Required when `merge_commit_message` is set. Valid combinations: (PR_TITLE, PR_BODY), (PR_TITLE, BLANK), (MERGE_MESSAGE, PR_TITLE).

merge_commit_message.description: The default message for a merge commit. `PR_BODY` uses the pull request's body. `PR_TITLE` uses the pull request's title. `BLANK` results in a blank commit message. Valid combinations with merge_commit_title: (PR_TITLE, PR_BODY), (PR_TITLE, BLANK), (MERGE_MESSAGE, PR_TITLE).

delete_branch_on_merge.description: Whether to automatically delete head branches when pull requests are merged.

squash_merge_commit_title.description: The default title for a squash merge commit. `PR_TITLE` uses the pull request's title. `COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE` uses the commit's title (if only one commit) or the pull request's title (if multiple commits).

squash_merge_commit_message.description: The default message for a squash merge commit. `PR_BODY` uses the pull request's body. `COMMIT_MESSAGES` uses the branch's commit messages. `BLANK` results in a blank commit message.

GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY.description: Retrieves detailed information about an existing and accessible GitHub repository.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is case-insensitive.

owner.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is case-insensitive.

GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES.description: Tool to atomically create, update, or delete multiple files in a GitHub repository as a single commit. Uses Git Data APIs to avoid SHA mismatch conflicts that occur with the Contents API when multiple files are modified in parallel. Use when you need to make multi-file changes reliably. BRANCH CREATION: When committing to a new branch (e.g., 'fix/my-fix' or 'feature/new-feature'), you MUST provide 'base_branch' (typically 'main' or 'master') to create the branch from. If the branch already exists, base_branch is not needed. This action handles race conditions automatically: if the branch is updated by another commit between fetching the HEAD and updating the reference (resulting in a 422 'not a fast forward' error), the action will retry by refetching the HEAD and rebasing changes. Use max_retries to control this behavior.

force.description: Force update the branch reference. WARNING: Use with caution as this can overwrite commits. Only use this when you intentionally want to overwrite the branch history.

date.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for the commit (optional, defaults to current time)

name.description: Name of the author or committer

email.description: Email address of the author or committer

branch.description: Target branch name to commit to. If this branch doesn't exist, you MUST provide 'base_branch' to create it. For new feature branches (e.g., 'fix/my-fix', 'feature/new-feature'), always set base_branch='main' (or your default branch).

deletes.description: List of file paths to delete from the repository. Files must exist in the repository; attempting to delete non-existent files will result in an error. Ensure paths are exact with no leading/trailing whitespace.

path.description: File path in the repository (e.g., 'src/main.py' or 'docs/readme.md')

encoding.description: Content encoding: 'utf-8' for text files or 'base64' for binary files

items.description: Represents a file to create or update.

upserts.description: List of files to create or update. Each entry requires path, content, and optional encoding (utf-8 or base64)

date.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for the commit (optional, defaults to current time)

name.description: Name of the author or committer

email.description: Email address of the author or committer

base_branch.description: REQUIRED when committing to a new branch that doesn't exist yet. Specifies the existing branch to create the new branch from (e.g., 'main' or 'master'). Not needed if 'branch' already exists in the repository.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retries when encountering race conditions (422 'not a fast forward' errors). The action will refetch the HEAD and rebase changes on each retry. Set to 0 to disable retries.

GITHUB_UPDATE_A_REPOSITORY.description: Updates settings for an existing GitHub repository, such as name, description, visibility, merge strategies, and security configurations.

name.description: New name for the repository (not case-sensitive).

repo.description: ACTUAL name of an existing repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive). MUST be a real repository that exists and is accessible - placeholder values like 'your-repo-name' will cause 404 errors.

owner.description: ACTUAL GitHub username or organization name that owns the repository (not case-sensitive). MUST be a real, existing account - placeholder values like 'your-username' will cause 404 errors.

private.description: Whether the repository is private. IMPORTANT: Public forks cannot be made private - this is a GitHub platform restriction. Changing visibility may also be restricted by organization policies.

archived.description: Archives the repository (making it read-only) or unarchives it.

has_issues.description: Enables GitHub Issues for this repository.

visibility.description: Repository visibility. IMPORTANT: Public forks cannot be made private - this is a GitHub platform restriction.

examples: A library for advanced data processing.

is_template.description: Designates this repository as a template repository.

has_projects.description: Enables GitHub Projects. Note: Organization settings might override this and cause an error if projects are disabled organization-wide.

allow_forking.description: Allows private forks of this repository. IMPORTANT: This setting can ONLY be changed for organization-owned repositories. Attempting to set this for user-owned repositories will result in a 422 error. Omit this field if you don't want to change the forking setting.

allow_merge_commit.description: Allows merging pull requests via merge commits.

merge_commit_title.description: Default title for merge commits: 'PR_TITLE' or 'MERGE_MESSAGE'. CONSTRAINT: If set to 'PR_TITLE', merge_commit_message must be 'PR_BODY' or 'BLANK'. If set to 'MERGE_MESSAGE', merge_commit_message must be blank/unset.

allow_update_branch.description: Allows updating a pull request's head branch from the base branch if not strictly required for merging.

merge_commit_message.description: Default message for merge commits: 'PR_BODY', 'PR_TITLE', or 'BLANK'. CONSTRAINT: If merge_commit_title is 'PR_TITLE', this must be 'PR_BODY' or 'BLANK'. Cannot be set when merge_commit_title is 'MERGE_MESSAGE'.

delete_branch_on_merge.description: Automatically deletes head branches after merging pull requests.

squash_merge_commit_title.description: Default title for squash merge commits: 'PR_TITLE' or 'COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE'.

squash_merge_commit_message.description: Default message for squash merge commits: 'PR_BODY', 'COMMIT_MESSAGES', or 'BLANK'.

web_commit_signoff_required.description: Requires contributors to sign off on web-based commits.

use_squash_pr_title_as_default.description: DEPRECATED: Use `squash_merge_commit_title`. If true, squash merge commits use PR title; otherwise, commit message.

security__and__analysis__secret__scannin.description: Manages secret scanning. Set to 'enabled' or 'disabled'.

security__and__analysis__advanced__secur.description: Manages GitHub Advanced Security. Set to 'enabled' or 'disabled'.

security__analysis__secret__scanning__pu.description: Manages secret scanning push protection. Set to 'enabled' or 'disabled'.

GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT.description: Retrieves a file's Base64 encoded content or lists a directory's contents from a GitHub repository.

ref.description: The name of the commit, branch, or tag to read from. Use this parameter to specify which branch (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main', 'develop'), tag (e.g., 'v1.2.0'), or commit SHA you want to access. If not provided, the repository's default branch will be used. Note: Branch names should be passed here, NOT in the path parameter.

path.description: Required. Path to file or directory in the repository. Empty string ('') retrieves root directory contents. Leading slashes auto-stripped. CRITICAL: Do NOT pass branch names here (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main'). Branch names belong in the `ref` parameter. Path should be file/directory path only (e.g., 'src/main.js', 'README.md'), NOT prefixed with branch name (use 'src/main.js' not 'main/src/main.js'). File paths must include extension (e.g., 'README.md', not 'README'). For common files (README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG) without extensions, action auto-tries common extensions (.md, .txt, .rst). Paths are case-sensitive. On 404 errors, list parent directory to verify exact path/casing.

repo.description: Required. The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

owner.description: Required. The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive. Can also accept full repository path in format 'owner/repo' - the repo part will be extracted automatically.

GITHUB_LIST_REPOSITORIES_FOR_THE_AUTHENT.description: Lists repositories for the authenticated user; using 'type' with 'visibility' or 'affiliation' API parameters (not in this model) can cause a 422 error.

page.description: Page number of results to fetch.

sort.description: The repository property by which to sort the results.

type.description: Filters the results to repositories of the specified type.

since.description: Filters for repositories updated at or after this specified time. Provide as an ISO 8601 formatted timestamp.

before.description: Filters for repositories updated before this specified time. Provide as an ISO 8601 formatted timestamp.

per_page.description: The number of results to return per page (maximum 100).

direction.description: The direction of the sort. Defaults to `asc` when `sort` is 'full_name', and `desc` otherwise.
